bc.title: Performing Fire — The Broadcast
bc.footer.tagline: Y = f(X) + ε · MOST SYSTEMS REDUCE ε. WE PERFORM IT.
bc.about.1.label: 01 / EQUATION
bc.about.1.heading: Y = f(X) + ε
bc.about.1.body: X is what people bring. f(X) is the system's attempt to organize it. ε is what will not stay put.
bc.about.2.label: 02 / INPUT
bc.about.2.heading: X / TRACES
bc.about.2.body: People bring messages, voices, drawings, gestures, movements, hopes, fears, and short videos. These traces are X: the raw material.
bc.about.3.label: 03 / MAP
bc.about.3.heading: f(X) / THE MAP
bc.about.3.body: The proposed system embeds, clusters, and maps the traces. f(X) is its attempt to make them legible and manageable.
bc.about.4.label: 04 / REMAINDER
bc.about.4.heading: ε / WHAT RESISTS
bc.about.4.body: Mistranslations, contradictions, silence, strange gestures, and unclear signals resist the map. Most AI systems reduce ε. Here, we perform it.
bc.about.5.label: 05 / PERFORMANCE
bc.about.5.heading: THE REMAINDER BURNS
bc.about.5.body: A performer works inside or around the fabric totem, changing ε into light, particles, sound, glitch, and symbolic fire.
bc.contribute.1.label: 01 / WHAT TO SEND
bc.contribute.1.heading: LEAVE A TRACE
bc.contribute.1.body: Send a question, hope, fear, or imagination about technology. The text form is live; voice and video are interface studies and do not upload media.
bc.contribute.2.label: 02 / WHAT HAPPENS
bc.contribute.2.heading: TRACE → MAP → ε
bc.contribute.2.body: Your trace joins the work's input. The proposed pipeline maps it; what resists that map becomes material for performance.

bc.contribute.3.heading: BEFORE TRANSMISSION
bc.contribute.3.note: SUBMISSIONS WAIT FOR MODERATION BEFORE PUBLICATION

bc.research.1.label: 01 / SOURCE REGISTRY
bc.research.1.heading: WHAT ENTERS THE CORPUS
bc.research.1.body: The Performing Fire corpus is organized as a source registry: Nam June Paik Art Center records, the separate Video Archive, the Video Library, the official Nam June Paik Art Center YouTube channel, and the ANTIEGG Fluxus article. Each entry is named before it is selected.
bc.research.2.label: 02 / BOUNDS
bc.research.2.heading: METADATA, NOT A MEDIA DUMP
bc.research.2.body: The working corpus keeps bounded public metadata and source links. Raw clips, images, and private material stay out of the repository.
bc.research.3.label: 03 / GOVERNANCE
bc.research.3.heading: RIGHTS CHANGE BY OPERATION
bc.research.3.body: Viewing, quoting, deriving, and publishing are separate operations. A source can be searchable for research without being copied, transformed, or published.
bc.research.4.label: 04 / PROVENANCE
bc.research.4.heading: SEARCH WITH A TRACE
bc.research.4.body: Search follows provenance—source, operation, and status—before a deliberate selection is made for a visual study. The result is a considered subset, not an automatic dump.
bc.research.5.label: 05 / STATE
bc.research.5.heading: HELD / OFFLINE / PROVEN
bc.research.5.body: Uncleared material stays held. Implemented offline means local metadata and fixtures only. Live-proven means a public path has been checked; research status never implies a finished model.

exp.microsite.title: THE BROADCAST AS MATERIAL
exp.microsite.body: The microsite studies what can carry a signal: TV-like containers, water, data totems, moon jars, and stupa forms.
exp.microsite.note: NJP objects and the cyberpunk columbarium were references; the direction is a modular wall of containers.
